text:
sam: Heads-up: nightly perf job flagged a regression after we merged Triton 2.4.1 build change. Small-batch (batch_size<=4, seq<=8) p50 latency +12% on A100 pools. Rollout blocked. Perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood.internal/d/serving/nightly-smallbatch

ci-bot: CI perf alert: nightly/serving-runtime-smallbatch exceeded threshold. Job: perf/nightly-smallbatch — baselines breached. Full report: https://ci.redwood.internal/reports/1970012345

maria: is this the triton patch that changed kernel selection heuristics? @alex did you see the PR?

alex: yep PR #876 changed autotune map + added new heuristics for matmul tiling. started a bisect — earliest bad = the autotune heuristic commit included in 2.4.1 release tag.

jordan: ran `nvprof` on the failing workload — matmul kernels show ~1.3x higher runtime for small N. snippet below:

```
== Profile result ==
Kernel: matmul_small_N
Time(μs): baseline 120 -> current 160
Occupancy: 64% -> 48%
Registers used: +24
Spill stores: 0 -> 18
```

ben: also seeing increased memcpy stalls around prefetch. KV cache fetch latency distribution shifted. `prefetch_wait_ms` p95 2.1 -> 6.3. traces: https://logs.redwood.internal/kv/prefetch/1970012345

alex: I suspect the tiling change increases register pressure, causing spills to local memory and worse occupancy for small batches. Triton autotune likely selected a variant optimized for larger tiles which hurts small N.

sam: Can we force old kernel selection for small N as a quick mitigation? /cc @maria

maria: Pushed a quick patch to runtime to add explicit override: if seq_len<=8 and batch<=4 prefer `matmul_small_v2`. Patch in branch `hotfix/smallbatch-matmul-policy`. Relevant diff: 

```python
# runtime/dispatch/kernel_policy.py (excerpt)
if seq_len <= 8 and batch_size <= 4:
    policy.preferred_kernels.insert(0, "matmul_small_v2")
```

ci-bot: Smoke test triggered for `hotfix/smallbatch-matmul-policy`: runtime unit tests + smallbatch perf harness.

jordan: Quick perf run on canary (A100 canary pool): p50 back to baseline, p95 improved vs current. No regressions observed on large-batch throughput in smoke runs. This looks promising as a short-term mitigation.

sam: Decision: hold Triton 2.4.1 rollout for hosted pools and block Dedicated rollout until this is resolved. Ops: pin images to Triton 2.4.0 for production pools until we have an upstream fix or runtime autotune adjustment. @ben can you open a revert PR + release note?

ben: On it. Drafting PR #882 to revert the autotune heuristic commit and adding the profiling notes + reproducer. I'll also add a postmortem checklist item to validate small-batch perf on future autotune changes.

alex: :thumbsup: I'll open an upstream Triton issue with a minimal repro and attach our nvprof traces and kernel disassembly. We should also consider adding a small-batch perf gate to the autotune CI.

sam: Thanks everyone. Keeping this thread as the rollout blocker tracker. If hotfix holds in canary for 24h we'll prepare the revert + patch rollout windows.
